I wake up at four in the morning and just lie there, staring at the ceiling, unable to fall back asleep. My head feels stuffed with cotton; I lose track of what I was saying, and it’s hard to follow conversations. Sometimes I catch myself thinking it wouldn’t be so bad if I just didn’t wake up one of these mornings, though I’m not planning to do anything.  

Things from the past still bother me, too—some memories I’d rather not talk about—but I’m not sure how it all fits together.
